name: Sideroblastic Anemia

criteria.description: Presence of ringed sideroblasts in bone marrow aspirate
Microcytic, hypochromic anemia on peripheral blood smear
Evidence of systemic iron overload (elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation)
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with sideroblastic anemia (e.g., ALAS2, SLC25A38)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ringed sideroblasts in bone marrow plus microcytic hypochromic anemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and iron studies support diagnosis and classification

pathognomonic.notes: Diagnostic hallmark seen on Prussian blue staining

searchTerms: anemia with small, light-colored red cells
chronic fatigue due to low red cells

common.symptomName: Pallor of skin and mucous membranes

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to iron overload
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems due to iron

occasional.symptomName: Neuropathy due to vitamin B6 deficiency
searchTerms: nerve damage from vitamin B6 lack
peripheral neuropathy due to B6 deficiency
tingling and numbness from low B6
yellowing of skin from red cell breakdown
skin and eye yellowing due to destroyed red cells

rare.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to pancreatic iron deposition
searchTerms: blood sugar problems due to iron buildup

rare.symptomName: Congestive heart failure due to iron cardiomyopathy
searchTerms: heart failure from iron heart disease
fluid buildup due to iron cardiomyopathy
weak heart pumping from iron overload

laboratory: Presence of ringed sideroblasts in bone marrow aspirate
Microcytic hypochromic anemia on peripheral smear
Elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation
Low pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6) levels in some cases
imaging: MRI T2* imaging for quantification of tissue iron deposition
genetic: Mutations in ALAS2 gene (X-linked sideroblastic anemia)
Mutations in SLC25A38 gene (autosomal recessive forms)
Other mitochondrial and nuclear gene mutations
other: Prussian blue staining of bone marrow biopsy highlighting ringed sideroblasts

distinguishingFeatures: Low serum ferritin and iron levels
No ringed sideroblasts in bone marrow
Dysplastic changes in multiple hematopoietic lineages

redFlags: Progressive anemia refractory to standard therapy
Evidence of systemic iron overload causing organ damage
Development of cardiac arrhythmias or heart failure
references: Cazzola M, et al. Sideroblastic anemia. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2017;2017(1): 1-9.
Molecular Genetics of Sideroblastic Anemia, OMIM 300751
